source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Board-of-nursing discipline is possible and may include remediation, restrictions, suspension, or revocation depending on law and the facts.","B":"The consequence is limited to employer counseling because Nurse Practice Acts are not enforced by boards of nursing.","C":"A scope violation automatically produces permanent license revocation regardless of severity or jurisdiction.","D":"A scope violation automatically produces a criminal conviction before any regulatory investigation occurs."}}
source_row.rationale: Boards of nursing enforce Nurse Practice Acts to protect the public. NCSBN describes disciplinary actions that may include remediation, restrictions, suspension, or revocation; the exact sanction depends on state law and the facts of the case.
source_row.source_detail: Board disciplinary actions may restrict practice, suspend a license, or revoke/surrender a license Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A nurse practices outside the legal scope authorized by the applicable Nurse Practice Act. Which consequence is possible?
